correctness.rationale: A circular three-gram histogram is a nonnegative balanced integer flow on the four-vertex order-two binary de Bruijn graph. Balance forces (h000,h001,h010,h011,h100,h101,h110,h111)=(a,t,t+f-s,s,t,f,s,h), c=t+f-s>=0, p=a+2t+f, q=h+t+s+f. The positive support admits an Eulerian closed walk exactly when connected. Five disjoint cases (t=s=0 with three connected types; t>0,s=0; t=0,s>0; t,s>0 with t>=s; t,s>0 with s>t) enumerate feasible flows via geometric series, yielding the displayed bivariate and length series. The pole order five gives n^4/288. Direct count of necklaces vs histograms n<=6 proves first collision, and zero-run padding gives distinct colliding necklaces for every n>=6. Independently enumerated binary words/fixed-content histograms through n14 and padded collisions through n25, matching first 14 coefficients; general theorem follows the connected-flow case proof, not finite tests.

originality.rationale: Classical de Bruijn Euler-flow sufficiency (Arnoux 2016), linear k-abelian classes (Karhumäki et al.) and first-order cyclic Markov types (Jacquet et al.) are prior work. The full 2016 Cassaigne–Karhumäki–Puzynina–Whiteland proceedings discusses linear k-abelian equivalence and rationality; its asymptotic class-count for a different boundary convention has degree six, not this degree-four circular full three-gram count. No inspected published work directly states the fixed-content rational function or the sharp necklace collision threshold, though stronger general all-gram flow enumeration might imply the result and remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Earlier general Markov-type methods could produce a stronger cyclic order-two count implicitly, or unindexed tables could report the same rational function.
Complete histogram counting does not determine sizes of all necklace preimages and does not address noisy, incomplete or length>3 reads.

value.rationale: Complete circular three-gram multiplicity is a natural exact information model for reconstruction from read histograms. A fixed-composition rational generating function, sharp class-count asymptotic and exact zero-error necklace-code size/first collision boundary answer more than the generic Eulerian realizability criterion. The fact is self-contained and useful for combinatorics on words and sequence reconstruction.

final_claim: For binary circular words with prescribed p zeros and q ones, the eight cyclic three-gram count vectors have an explicit bivariate rational generating function and length-only series, with A_n=n^4/288+O(n^3); necklace reconstruction injective exactly through length five, with a unique length-six collision and collisions at all longer lengths.
limitations: Earlier general Markov-type methods could produce a stronger cyclic order-two count implicitly, or unindexed tables could report the same rational function.
Complete histogram counting does not determine sizes of all necklace preimages and does not address noisy, incomplete or length>3 reads.
